papers.title: EagleVLA: Onboard Real-Time Control via Asynchronous Inference
papers.authorship_status: From the attributed catalogue; accepted-version verification remains separate.
papers.summary: EagleVLA targets onboard real-time control where cloud latency or limited edge compute can make action predictions stale. It combines future-state anticipation with asynchronous inference and scheduling so a robot can react to more recent observations while maintaining coherent motion. The talk evaluates control frequency, observation-action alignment and real-world task execution, not just raw model throughput.

papers.title: REACT: Rolling Denoising for Reactive VLA Control
papers.authorship_status: From the attributed catalogue; accepted-version verification remains separate.
papers.summary: REACT addresses a latency-versus-smoothness trade-off in action-chunking policies. Longer chunks produce coherent motion but can become outdated when objects move; shorter chunks react faster but may be jittery. Rolling denoising revises an ongoing action sequence using fresh observations, allowing the controller to respond without discarding all temporal consistency. It is a reactive-control method, not agentic self-improvement.

papers.title: TARC: Time-Adaptive Robotic Control
papers.authorship_status: From the attributed catalogue; accepted-version verification remains separate.
papers.summary: TARC turns the control-update rate into a learned decision. Instead of replanning at a fixed frequency, a policy selects both an action and how long to hold it, subject to an explicit update budget. The talk applies this idea to locomotion and VLA-style control, asking when expensive inference is actually necessary to retain successful feedback control.
papers.summary_basis: Editorial paraphrase from the supplied automatic recorded-talk transcript.

papers.title: Diffusion ReRoll: Revisable Denoising
papers.authorship_status: From the attributed catalogue; accepted-version verification remains separate.
papers.summary: Diffusion ReRoll changes how denoising progresses across time in robot sequence prediction. Conventional full-horizon and causal schedules can commit early to a poor motion prefix; partial re-noising keeps earlier and later steps open to revision. The speaker reports stronger sequence behavior on challenging trajectories and argues that the noise schedule itself is a useful temporal inductive bias.

papers.summary: MoRE proposes a mixture-of-motion-experts design for 3D world models spanning different material and actuator dynamics. papers.summary: This paper studies a security failure mode of robot-learning pipelines that use third-party demonstrations and generative world models. An attacker perturbs seemingly ordinary visual inputs so the world model generates undesirable behavior under an otherwise benign task prompt; training on those generations can contaminate the downstream policy. The result is a warning about data provenance and model-mediated amplification, not an endorsed attack technique.

papers.summary: Chunk-wise Model-based Policy Optimization replaces repeated one-step imagined rollouts with a model that predicts a future latent chunk from the current state and a proposed action chunk. The goal is to obtain useful multi-step optimization signals while reducing recursive model error and backpropagation-through-time instability. The talk reports simulation and bipedal-control experiments; numerical comparisons remain speaker-reported.

papers.title: FedGuide: Federated Reinforcement Learning
